name: Blind requestioning of the development sets
policy: Rewordings were written by a model given only the questions (and any case text), with no tools, files or repository access. Each was judged to ask the same thing before any engine run; rejected rewordings are excluded. Every rewording keeps its original expected answer. No author repairs or additional premises are permitted during evaluation.

cases.question: May the Line Lead begin order A17-P at 11:00, and whose further action is still needed to lift the moisture hold?
cases.case: Lot Aster-17 arrived at 09:10 with 42 kilograms of seed, received a moisture hold after a first-sample result of 8.6 percent, and had a second-sample result of 7.8 percent recorded by the Quality Examiner at 10:40. At 11:00 all 42 kilograms remained in the lot, the Stock Controller had not removed the hold or set aside the reserve, and the Label Clerk had approved the proof for the intended packing order A17-P.

evidenceAll: The Stock Controller may remove a moisture hold only after the Quality Examiner records a moisture result of 8.0 percent or less from a second sample of the same lot.
A second-sample moisture result of 8.0 percent or less recorded by the Quality Examiner permits the Stock Controller to remove the moisture hold but does not automatically remove that hold.
The Line Lead may start a packing order only after the Stock Controller has removed all holds on its seed lot and the Label Clerk has approved its label proof.

cases.requestionedFrom: At 11:00, may the Line Lead start order A17-P, and whose action is still needed to clear the moisture hold?

cases.question: At 11:00, may Reed-26 be cancelled by the Packing Superintendent?
cases.case: For order Reed-26, the Line Lead recorded the first sealed packet at 10:05 and stopped the line at 10:40 after finding a torn seal. A replacement sealing jaw was then fitted, the Seal Inspector examined five consecutive packets at 10:55 and found all five seals intact, and the Seal Inspector recorded a passed check at 10:56.

evidenceAll: The Packing Superintendent may cancel a packing order before the Line Lead records the first sealed packet, but must not cancel the order after that record is made.
